classification.difficultyReason: Combine all four goat regions and use the complement within 120 students, recognising that the missing horse-only count need not be recovered.

content.prompt:
A school surveyed 120 of its students about the type of animals they have at home. The results are recorded in the Venn diagram below, although the number of students who only own horses is missing.

If one of the students is selected at random, what is the probability that the student does not own a goat?

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular universal-set frame with Dog above Horse and Goat. The Horse-only region remains blank; no universal-set label is printed.
spec.mathematics: Dog only 41; Horse only unknown; Goat only 20; Dog and Horse only 15; Dog and Goat only 9; Horse and Goat only 4; all three 7; outside all sets 8. Total 120.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied region counts appear in the question diagram. The missing Horse-only count and probability are withheld.

answer.worked: $\begin{aligned}\text{Students who own a goat} &= 20+9+4+7=40\\\text{Students who do not own a goat} &= 120-40=80\\P(\text{does not own a goat}) &= \frac{80}{120}=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$
